cards.explanation: The answer is accuse. The text says Satan is standing at Joshua's right hand "…to accuse him." (Zechariah 3:1). He didn't show up for small talk, friends. Joshua is the high priest, and Satan is right there at his side, ready to point a finger.

The answer is "The LORD rebukes you." The LORD says, "The LORD rebukes you, Satan!" (Zechariah 3:2). Satan is there to accuse, and the LORD is the one who speaks up, friends. Then He asks, "Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?" (Zechariah 3:2).

The answer is False. The text says Joshua "…was dressed in filthy garments…" as he stood before the angel (Zechariah 3:3). That's a rough outfit for a high priest, friends. I've worn dust and drawer lint myself, so I'm not judging.

The answer is "Take off his filthy clothes." The angel says to those standing before him, "Take off his filthy clothes!" (Zechariah 3:4). Joshua doesn't have to scrub himself clean, friends. Somebody else takes the dirty clothes off him.
The answer is sin. The angel tells Joshua, "See, I have removed your iniquity…" (Zechariah 3:4). Iniquity means sin, friends, and it's gone. It was lifted off Joshua, not earned back by him.
The answer is True. The angel says, "…I will clothe you with splendid robes." (Zechariah 3:4). Filthy clothes come off and something splendid goes on, friends. That's a big upgrade.

The answer is clean. Zechariah says, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." (Zechariah 3:5). Then a clean turban was placed on Joshua's head. He's been wearing filthy garments, friends, so clean is exactly the word.

The answer is walk in His ways and keep His instructions. The angel of the LORD gives Joshua a charge from the LORD of Hosts: "If you walk in My ways and keep My instructions…" (Zechariah 3:7). Notice that this comes right after Joshua's clothes are changed, friends. That's a big job, and I'm glad it came after the new robes.

The answer is True. The LORD of Hosts says, "…I will give you a place among these who are standing here." (Zechariah 3:7). Joshua started this scene with an accuser at his side, friends. Now he's promised a spot among those standing there.

The answer is True. The LORD of Hosts says, "…I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day." (Zechariah 3:9). Joshua's iniquity was already removed in verse 4, friends. Now the promise gets bigger, from one man to the whole land.

The answer is to sit under your own vine and fig tree. The LORD of Hosts says, "…you will each invite your neighbor to sit under your own vine and fig tree." (Zechariah 3:10). Picture neighbors waving each other over to sit down, friends. I like this picture a lot.
